clue.text: Diagram produced by graduate of building design with skill

parts.note: a BArch is a Bachelor of Architecture degree, held by a graduate in building design
art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: Someone trained in architecture skilfully produces a diagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart drawn with bars of varying length is a common kind of statistical diagram.

clue.text: Hollow Conservative greeting

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail

explanation.surface: A Tory offers an empty, insincere hello.
explanation.definitionFit: A cave is a natural hollow in rock or a hillside.

clue.text: Treasurer making sort of appeal in regional accent

indicators.note: in places the appeal letters within the accent word

parts.note: a burr is a rough rolled-R regional accent, as in the West Country
SA is sex appeal, one sort of appeal

explanation.surface: A college treasurer pleads for money in a local accent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar manages the finances of a college or school, acting as its treasurer.

clue.text: French fortress to keep wet in hot conditions, bad inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the word for bad goes within the cooking word

parts.words: to keep wet in hot conditions
parts.note: to baste is to keep roasting meat moist by spooning fat over it in the oven
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: A prison fortress where inmates are kept damp and hot, with bad conditions within.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-prison stormed in 1789 at the start of the French Revolution.

clue.text: I get lost and I start to panic terribly and flap

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to getting lost, panicking badly and getting into a flap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' looks like part of the panic story, but it is the definition; the letters of I GET LOST, I and P (from 'start to panic') are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The epiglottis is a flap of cartilage that covers the windpipe during swallowing.

clue.text: Wasting time, let's observe tenant

indicators.note: wasting means losing or getting rid of, so the time letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
to see is to observe

explanation.surface: A landlord says: let's not waste time, look at the tenant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee holds property under a lease, so is a tenant of the owner.

clue.text: South American country fellow crossing Austria behind soldier

indicators.note: behind puts the fellow piece after the soldier

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the fellow wraps the Austria letter

parts.note: guy is an informal word for a fellow
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A man trailing a soldier across Austria heads for South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraguay is a landlocked republic in central South America.

clue.text: Language of a lad brought up outside Rugby

indicators.note: outside means the reversed lad phrase sits around the rugby letters
in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a boy is a lad
RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A boy raised in a rugby-playing setting speaks a particular tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses A BOY to give YOBA, which is placed 'outside' RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoruba is a language spoken by millions in south-western Nigeria and Benin.

clue.text: Fruit drinks including pop devoid of content

indicators.note: including means the drinks word holds the other letters within it

parts.note: ales are beers, drinks

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: Fruit-flavoured drinks with fizzy pop that tastes of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Apples are the familiar orchard fruit.

clue.text: Area in the grip of maniac recently

indicators.note: held tightly by the words that follow, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A small region has lately fallen into the hands of a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, about 4,047 square metres.

clue.text: It's great new street — result of one making long-term plan

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A town planner boasts of a fine new road built to a long-term scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist is someone who devises long-range plans, especially in war or business.

clue.text: Moister bread?

definitions.meaning: an Australian unleavened bread traditionally baked in the ashes of a campfire

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the less familiar second sense: damper is Australian bush bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Damper is both the comparative of damp and the name of a simple Australian soda bread.

clue.text: Fussy person not half — devil to get changed yet

indicators.note: taking only half of the word, its first three letters

parts.note: Old Nick is a name for the devil

indicators.note: the letters of the word are to be altered, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A particular person complains the devil has yet to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get changed' rearranges YET into ETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pernickety is excessively particular about small details, i.e. fussy.

clue.text: Famous inventor was in debt and shouted

parts.note: Alexander Graham Bell, inventor of the telephone
owed means was in debt

explanation.surface: A celebrated inventor, deep in debt, yelled about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bellowed is to have roared or shouted loudly.

clue.text: Tax row in which artist suffers setback

indicators.note: in which tells us the quarrel word holds the artist inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a small quarrel, a row

indicators.note: set back means turned backwards, so the artist letters are reversed

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter loses out in an argument over taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax or duty, especially one charged on imports.

clue.text: Female with formality and with frostiness

parts.note: rigidly means stiffly, with strict formality

explanation.surface: A woman behaves formally and coldly.
explanation.definitionFit: Frigidly means in a cold, frosty manner, literally or in attitude.

clue.text: Like an astronaut made fun of

explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is launched skywards, and to mock someone in parody is to lampoon them; the phrase covers both.

clue.text: Denim top manufactured somewhere in Italy

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: A denim top was made in an Italian region.
explanation.definitionFit: Piedmont is a region of north-west Italy with Turin as its capital.

clue.text: Buried under food shop is American composer

indicators.note: in a down clue the American piece lies below the shop piece

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop
US is short for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: An American lies buried beneath a delicatessen.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick Delius was an English composer, known for orchestral pieces such as On Hearing the First Cuckoo in Spring.

clue.text: Humourless-looking model, I have to create an image

parts.note: po as in po-faced, wearing a humourless expression
to sit for an artist is to model
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A stern-faced model says she has to strike a pose for a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In photography a positive is the finished image, with true tones, printed from a negative.

clue.text: Old cad leading soldiers — one to stir them into action?

definitions.text: one to stir them into action?

indicators.note: leading means coming in front of the soldiers piece

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a cad
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: An old scoundrel commands troops and rouses them to fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker who rouses a crowd with stirring rhetoric is a public speaker of that kind.

clue.text: Restaurant offerings the man discovered in East Anglian town

indicators.note: found inside, so the man goes within the town name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, East Anglia
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man is found in a Norfolk town ordering from a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes are the prepared items of food a restaurant serves.

clue.text: Weapon spelling peril — good for ousting any number

indicators.note: the good letter takes the place of the number letter, driving it out

parts.note: danger means peril
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A weapon spells trouble, and goodness drives out the multitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' is a link word meaning signifying.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagger is a short stabbing weapon.

clue.text: Returning soldiers will be having an undesired effect

parts.note: back means returning, as in coming back
soldiers in action will be shooting their weapons

explanation.surface: Soldiers who return will be shooting, with unwelcome results.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that is backfiring rebounds on its maker, producing the opposite of what was intended.

clue.text: Swelling fruit, soft from one end to the other

indicators.text: from one end to the other
indicators.note: the soft letter shifts from the front of the word to its back

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
P is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Squashy fruit has a lump running right across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump is a bump or swelling on the body.

clue.text: Scottish landlord, heartless and fat

indicators.note: without its heart, so the central letter goes

parts.note: a laird is a Scottish landowner

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner is cruel and overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Human being ethical about trade primarily

indicators.note: about means around, so the ethical word surrounds the letter

parts.note: moral means ethical

indicators.note: primarily means first, so just the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: A principled person thinks hard about trade.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal is a human, as opposed to an immortal god.

clue.text: Feature of car that may arouse gent's ire

indicators.note: arouse suggests stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Something in a car's handling makes a man angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Steering is the mechanism that directs a car's wheels, a standard feature of a car.
